reflection_diagnosis.causal_diagnosis: The current reward achieves 80% success_like_terminal_rate with stable touchdowns, but the dense positive budget (1512.25) is much larger than the objective positive budget (82.4), giving a dense_to_objective_ratio of 0.21. The policy can accumulate large rewards by staying near the pad with low velocity and upright angle, without needing to terminate. This explains the 20% timeout rate where the policy hovers on the pad collecting dense rewards. The reward_payment_audit flags main_engine_firings and orientation_engine_firings as raw_action_bonus_terms, but these are diagnostic-only variables not part of the reward sum. The real issue is the dense_to_objective_ratio: the objective bonus is relatively too small compared to the dense progress rewards, so the policy prefers to delay termination to collect more dense rewards.
reflection_diagnosis.component_interaction_diagnosis: The dominant components by absolute return are orientation_engine_firings (315.2), main_engine_firings (284.0), distance_to_pad (268.47), both_legs_contact (179.6), vertical_speed_reward (168.36), distance_reward (146.47), success_bonus (80.0). The first four are diagnostic-only and not part of the reward sum. The actual reward components are balanced with no single component dominating (dominance_ratio 1.11 for orientation_engine_firings, but that's diagnostic). The dense positive budget (1512.25) is much larger than the objective positive budget (82.4), meaning the policy can accumulate large rewards by staying near the pad with low velocity and upright angle, without needing to terminate. This may explain why the policy sometimes times out (20% timeout rate) while collecting dense rewards on the pad.
reflection_diagnosis.action_coverage_diagnosis: All four discrete actions are used (coverage_ratio 1.0). The dominant action is 2 (main engine) at 41.6%, followed by 1 (left orientation) at 30.4%, 3 (right orientation) at 15.8%, and 0 (do nothing) at 12.3%. Since all actions are already used, the issue is not action coverage but trajectory-phase guidance: the policy learns to reach the pad and then stay there to collect dense rewards, rather than terminating quickly.
reflection_diagnosis.failed_pattern_reuse_check: Two failed patterns are explicitly forbidden: (1) Reducing distance_reward, vertical_speed_reward, and angle_reward scales (iter_002->iter_003 caused -23.96 fitness drop and regression to hovering). (2) Increasing success_bonus from 100 to 200 alone (iter_003->iter_004 caused -290.79 fitness drop and regression to hovering). The successful pattern (iter_000->iter_001) that improved fitness by +37.43 was converting the success_bonus from per-step to one-shot and conditioning engine penalties on both_legs_contact. That pattern is already implemented in the current reward. The current edit must avoid both failed patterns and instead address the dense_to_objective_ratio by a different mechanism.

search_decision.reason: Following expert_action_plan and search_mode_recommendation: payment_mode_rewrite is required to address the large dense positive budget relative to objective budget. The edit scope is small because we are only adding a one-shot early-termination bonus for landing quickly (time bonus at termination), which increases the relative attractiveness of terminating without reducing dense rewards or increasing the success_bonus alone. This avoids both forbidden patterns.

edit_summary.reason: Add a one-shot early-termination bonus (time_bonus) that pays at termination if the episode ended successfully and ended before a threshold (e.g., 500 steps). This increases the objective_positive_budget without reducing dense rewards or increasing the success_bonus alone. The bonus is event-gated (paid only at termination) and one-shot (paid once per episode). This makes termination relatively more attractive compared to collecting dense rewards, encouraging the policy to land quickly and terminate. The bonus is scaled to be comparable to the success_bonus (50 for early termination, 25 for medium termination) to provide a meaningful incentive without dominating.

changed_design: Added time_bonus: one-shot terminal bonus for early termination (50 if episode length < 500, 25 if episode length < 750, 0 otherwise). This is event-gated and one-shot, paid only at termination if success condition met.

edit_summary.action_coverage_plan: All four discrete actions remain available. The revised reward does not change action space. The policy should still use all actions for stabilization and descent. The main change is that the policy is now incentivized to terminate quickly after landing, which may reduce the use of action 0 (do nothing) while hovering on the pad.
edit_summary.phase_guidance_plan: Phase 1 (approach): distance_reward (max 0.5) and vertical_speed_reward (max 0.3) still guide descent. Phase 2 (descent): engine penalties remain mild and conditioned on not being landed. Phase 3 (touchdown): success_bonus (100) and time_bonus (up to 50) are now both available at termination, encouraging the policy to complete the episode quickly after landing.
edit_summary.payment_mode_plan: success_bonus: one-shot terminal event (paid only at termination if success condition met). time_bonus: one-shot terminal event (paid only at termination if success condition met and episode length < threshold). main_engine_penalty: progress-conditioned (reduced when both legs contact). orientation_engine_penalty: progress-conditioned (reduced when both legs contact). distance_reward, vertical_speed_reward, angle_reward: per-step but bounded and small relative to objective.
